note: Static suspects only. A finding becomes CONFIRMED only with a profile or reproduction. One was confirmed and fixed: contact export whole-file gzip/gunzip.

fixed.path: POST export (stream, then save) and GET download
fixed.workload: synthetic NDJSON 1/5/20/50 MB; export cap is EXPORT_MAX_ROWS=200000 rows
fixed.behaviorCheck: async gzip output byte-identical to gzipSync and round-trips, for empty to 23 MB inputs; bulk-and-filter.spec.ts 22/22 pass
fixed.userImpact: Every request in the API process stalls while a large export is saved or downloaded.
fixed.caveat: Synthetic data and a single machine; actual export byte sizes per row are not measured. The end-to-end API effect is NOT VERIFIED (needs the app with a database).
fixed.regressionTest: tools/event-loop-audit/scan.mjs --check (the gate fails if a sync zlib call returns to a runtime path in this file)

runtimeFindings.why: Synchronous compression blocks in proportion to payload size.
runtimeFindings.evidence: gzipSync/gunzipSync hold the loop ~14ms/MB and ~3.3ms/MB (docs/performance/event-loop/evidence/zlib-hold.json). Call site compresses a bounded batch (2k-20k rows), so real impact depends on row size: NOT CONFIRMED on production-shaped data.

runtimeFindings.why: CPU-heavy synchronous crypto runs on the main thread.
runtimeFindings.fix: Use the async variant (runs on the libuv pool).
runtimeFindings.evidence: hkdfSync derives a key from a short secret: microseconds. NOT a measured problem.

runtimeFindings.why: Synchronous filesystem call blocks every other request while the disk answers.
runtimeFindings.fix: Use fs/promises, or hoist to startup.
runtimeFindings.evidence: Runs at install/migration/locale-load time, not per request, or is cached: lower risk. NOT PROFILED.
